profile.campus: Hillsboro, Oregon (Flexential's Hillsboro data center campus, four existing buildings plus a fifth completed and a sixth planned as of 2025)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 4) is located at 4915 NE Starr Blvd, Hillsboro, OR 97124. The operator publishes a footprint of 138000 square feet and 36 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building is part of Flexential's wider Hillsboro campus, which Data Center Dynamics reported in 2025 had grown to five sites (four existing buildings plus Hillsboro 5, then under construction) totaling 1.18 million square feet and 113 megawatts of capacity, with a sixth facility then being planned across from Hillsboro 1 at 350,000 square feet and 27 megawatts. Flexential president and COO Ryan Mallory described Hillsboro as "a smart alternative to Silicon Valley for customers seeking the performance, flexibility, and cost structure they can't find elsewhere, especially those with strong ties across the Pacific." DCD also reported that the Hillsboro market ran extremely tight in the first half of 2025, with a vacancy rate of just 0.2% and 48.4 megawatts of absorption against 48 megawatts of new supply delivered, roughly 10% of total market inventory turning over in six months. Hillsboro sits in Oregon's "Silicon Forest" technology corridor west of Portland, built up around Intel's long-standing local manufacturing presence and the skilled workforce it created, a legacy that has also drawn other major data center operators, including Meta, to the same area.

The City of Hillsboro reports that, as of July 2026, the city hosted 23 total data center sites, 16 already constructed across 346 acres plus 7 more in permitting or under construction across another 224 acres, together occupying roughly 570 of the city's 17,378 total acres. In 2025, Hillsboro's data center sector generated about $61.1 million in total taxes; 12 entities receiving Enterprise Zone property-tax abatements held roughly $7.2 billion in exempted real market value, out of an $11 billion combined assessed/exempted value across all data centers in the city. Eligible facilities receive temporary property-tax abatement on new investment for three to five years under Hillsboro's Enterprise Zone program, after which standard property taxes apply, alongside application fees capped at $50,000 and Community Service Fees of up to 33% of abated taxes in the first three years. Statewide, Oregon's data center industry supported an estimated 9,310 direct jobs and 38,380 indirect and induced jobs, with more than $4.1 billion in labor income, in 2023, according to industry analysis cited by the city.

reading.body:
Flexential Portland – Hillsboro 4 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a typical enterprise average, the same power supports roughly 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is an illustrative range, not an operator claim. The floor plate is large enough that the binding constraint on AI workloads is almost certainly power density per rack rather than raw square footage.

The certification stack qualifies the campus for a wide range of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ITAR qualifies it for defense and export-controlled technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. SSAE 18 is the audit standard underlying the SOC reports. Which tenants actually occupy the facility is not published.

Among the 133 data center facilities mapped in Oregon, only six have published a megawatt figure on their operator pages, and those six together account for 182 MW of published IT capacity in the state. This campus, at 36 MW, ranks first among those six, representing roughly 20 percent of all published Oregon capacity this site has read. That figure reflects the limits of what operators have disclosed, not a census of Oregon's total installed power.
